sources.title: Admitted brief: Background extension task admission and fairness
sources.observed_operation: Read the exact brief directly before external source discovery.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Defines Windows/Linux desktop extension tasks, queue/fairness/resource/cancellation/progress/restart requirements, negative constraints and proposal-only scope.
sources.applicability: Direct governing input for this investigation.

sources.title: Job Objects — Win32 apps | Microsoft Learn
sources.released_version_or_commit: Windows desktop API reference; page last updated 2025-07-14; live documentation accessed 2026-10-12
sources.locator: Creating Jobs; Managing Processes in Jobs; Job Limits and Notifications; Managing Job Objects; Managing a Process Tree that Uses Job Objects
sources.observed_operation: Opened Microsoft Learn page and located process association/inheritance, termination and close semantics.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: CreateJobObject creates empty job; AssignProcessToJobObject attaches process and association cannot be broken. CreateProcess children normally inherit job, but Win32_Process.Create children do not; breakaway flags alter inheritance. TerminateJobObject affects associated members. Last handle close kills members only with KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE. Nested jobs supported starting Windows 8; older Windows versions support one job only.
sources.applicability: Candidate Windows per-task process-tree boundary; test assignment and host-in-job cases; not a complete security sandbox.

sources.title: JOBOBJECT_BASIC_LIMIT_INFORMATION — Win32 apps | Microsoft Learn
sources.released_version_or_commit: Windows desktop API reference; live page accessed 2026-10-12
sources.observed_operation: Opened current structure reference and inspected exact limit semantics.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_JOB_MEMORY caps job-wide sum of committed memory and blocks commits beyond limit; it is not a host-wide memory cap. KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE terminates members when last handle closes. PROCESS_MEMORY is per process, with most restrictive nested limit.
sources.applicability: Supports per-task resource/cancellation design and metric choice on Windows; validate runtime semantics in the target app.

sources.title: Control Group v2 — The Linux Kernel documentation
sources.locator: Memory controller, memory.current, memory.peak, memory.high, memory.max, memory.events and Delegation sections
sources.observed_operation: Opened version-pinned kernel documentation and inspected memory accounting, limit, peak and delegation text.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: memory.current counts cgroup and descendants, memory.peak tracks maximum since cgroup creation/reset; memory.high throttles/reclaims but may be breached and does not invoke OOM killer; memory.max is hard but may be exceeded temporarily and can invoke OOM kill inside the cgroup. Delegation requires permission and only distributes resources the parent made available; controllers are hierarchical.
sources.applicability: Candidate Linux per-task accounting/containment only if cgroup v2 memory controller is enabled and a writable delegated subtree exists.

sources.title: Control Group APIs and Delegation — systemd.io
sources.released_version_or_commit: Live systemd documentation; includes v256/v258 hierarchy history; accessed 2026-10-12
sources.locator: Single-writer rule; hierarchy support; Delegation; controller enablement
sources.observed_operation: Read systemd guidance on ownership/delegation and version-specific hierarchy transitions.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: cgroup v2 is governed by a single-writer rule; direct management outside the delegated subtree is not allowed. Delegate is available to services/scopes, but setting it makes requested controllers available without enabling them; enable memory in the delegated subtree. systemd documentation says legacy/hybrid hierarchies deprecated in v256 and removed in v258.
sources.applicability: Explains why Linux support must detect actual user delegation/controller availability rather than assume rootless hard limits.

sources.title: The New Control Group Interfaces — systemd.io
sources.locator: single-writer cgroup v2 statement; transient scope/service creation; delegation and accounting properties
sources.observed_operation: Read API guidance returned from official systemd search results.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: systemd exposes transient units over its manager API, controls the main tree, and allows explicitly delegated subtrees; resource accounting includes current/peak memory properties where supported.
sources.applicability: Alternative managed Linux worker lifecycle/monitoring route; support and privileges must be verified per user session.

sources.title: Semaphore in tokio::sync — Rust docs.rs
sources.released_version_or_commit: Tokio 1.53.2 shown in retrieved page on 2026-10-12; latest URL is mutable
sources.locator: Struct Semaphore overview; acquire_many; cancel safety
sources.observed_operation: Read published API contract for permits, FIFO behavior and acquire_many interactions.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Waiters receive permits in FIFO request order, including acquire_many; a large request at queue head can block smaller requests despite available permits. Cancelling acquire loses its position.
sources.applicability: Useful bounded-concurrency primitive example; does not persist tenant queue state, explain wait reasons, or enforce byte memory limits.

sources.title: Tokio semaphore implementation — release-tagged source
sources.released_version_or_commit: Tokio release tag tokio-1.53.2 (2026-10-03); source URL pinned to tag, commit SHA not resolved
sources.locator: module implementation comments and waiter queue; permit assignment and cancellation cleanup around lines 1-16, 280-355, 380-515, 570-611
sources.observed_operation: Opened raw source at exact release tag; reviewed linked waiter queue, FIFO order and drop cleanup behavior.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Implementation uses intrusive waiter list, places waiters at tail and assigns released permits from head; Acquire::drop removes waiter/returns assigned permits. This implementation governs Tokio's in-process semaphore, not durable host jobs.
sources.applicability: Inspected as a candidate primitive's real implementation, not selected as the task scheduler.

sources.title: Tokio semaphore tests — release-tagged source
sources.released_version_or_commit: Tokio release tag tokio-1.53.2 (2026-10-03); source URL pinned to tag
sources.locator: no_permits; try_acquire; acquire/add_permits; stress_test; permit operations
sources.observed_operation: Inspected release-tagged tests; no tests were executed.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Tests exercise permit accounting, acquiring after release, closing, permit merge/split, and 1000-waiter stress; these tests do not establish extension-level fairness, persistence, bytes limits, task cancellation, or restart guarantees.
sources.applicability: Bounded evidence for inspected candidate tests; a product scheduler needs additional host-specific validation.

sources.title: Fairness problem with semaphore acquire — Tokio issue #4612
sources.released_version_or_commit: Issue opened 2022-04-11; reports Tokio 1.17.0 on macOS; current issue page accessed 2026-10-12
sources.locator: issue body and status/relationship to issue #4624
sources.observed_operation: Opened issue page and read reproducer/context.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Reporter observes a spawned task not progressing when another task loops acquiring a permit without a cooperative yield; issue links to #4624. This is a runtime/task-cooperation report, not evidence of broken semaphore FIFO.
sources.applicability: Warns that an in-process async task/scheduler still needs cooperation and isolation; does not establish the host's implementation behavior.

sources.title: Efficient Fair Queueing Using Deficit Round-Robin
sources.released_version_or_commit: IEEE/ACM Transactions on Networking, vol. 4 no. 3, June 1996; paper first presented at SIGCOMM 1995
sources.locator: title, abstract and discussion of application to non-breakable service/load balancing
sources.observed_operation: Opened primary paper search result and reviewed bibliographic information and abstract.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: DRR approximates fair queuing across network flows using deficit accounting; paper says it can apply to non-breakable service such as load balancing. Its demonstrated domain is packet flows.
sources.applicability: Conceptual basis for comparing weighted extension turns; transfer to variable duration/memory jobs remains an inference requiring tests.

sources.title: Write-Ahead Logging — SQLite
sources.released_version_or_commit: Live SQLite documentation accessed 2026-10-12; WAL available since 3.7.0
sources.observed_operation: Opened official WAL documentation and inspected concurrency, constraints, checkpoint behavior and bug report.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: WAL permits reader/writer overlap but only one writer; all users must be on same host and WAL is unsupported over network filesystems. Checkpoint progress can be blocked by long readers. WAL-reset corruption bug affects concurrent write/checkpoint conditions through 3.51.2 and is fixed in 3.51.3+ and listed backports.
sources.applicability: Candidate embedded local queue ledger; pin/fix SQLite build and test WAL/recovery before adopting.

sources.title: SQLite Release History
sources.released_version_or_commit: Live release history; retrieved page shows SQLite 3.53.4 dated 2026-07-24 as top release
sources.observed_operation: Opened official release timeline; confirmed named fix and later release entries.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: 3.51.3 is the patch release that lists fixing WAL-reset corruption; 3.53.0 and subsequent 3.53 releases also include the fix. Version 3.52.0 was withdrawn, so do not select it as a baseline.
sources.applicability: Release gate for any WAL queue design: require fixed release/backport; verify the actual library bundled with the application.

sources.title: PRAGMA synchronous — SQLite
sources.locator: synchronous values FULL/NORMAL and WAL-mode behavior
sources.observed_operation: Opened official pragma reference and compared FULL versus NORMAL semantics.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: In WAL, NORMAL remains consistent but a just-committed transaction can roll back after system/power failure; FULL syncs the WAL at every commit, adding durability and I/O cost.
sources.applicability: Owner decision for queue-state durability/performance and crash-recovery semantics.

sources.title: Transaction — SQLite
sources.observed_operation: Read official transaction semantics returned by SQLite search.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: BEGIN IMMEDIATE starts a write transaction immediately and may fail SQLITE_BUSY if another writer is active; deferred read-to-write upgrade may fail later.
sources.applicability: Supports short transactional CAS/state transitions in an embedded local queue; caller still handles busy and never wraps long-running work in a transaction.

sources.title: Result and Error Codes — SQLite
sources.observed_operation: Read official SQLite concurrency/error guidance returned by search.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: SQLite supports one writer; concurrent write can yield SQLITE_BUSY. Busy timeout/handler are available; BEGIN IMMEDIATE can move the conflict to transaction start.
sources.applicability: Supports bounded busy/retry handling for short queue-state mutations.

sources.title: VS Code API — Visual Studio Code Extension API
sources.released_version_or_commit: Live VS Code extension API documentation accessed 2026-10-12
sources.observed_operation: Opened API reference for the host's user-facing progress/cancellation semantics.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Progress updates include increment/message and receive a CancellationToken; only notification progress supports cancel button and discrete progress according to the reference.
sources.applicability: UX/API precedent for cancellable progress; not a requirement or implementation dependency for the unnamed desktop host.

evidence_limitations: No target application's repository, callers, or tests were specified, so no app-specific source audit was possible.
Tokio released implementation and test files were inspected but not executed; Tokio is an alternative primitive, not an assumed target runtime.
The DRR-to-job scheduling transfer is an inference from the paper's packet-flow design and non-breakable-service note.
No Windows/Linux machine was queried for actual support/capabilities and no performance/load/crash tests were run.
